body.statement: For every \(0<\beta<1\) and \(0\le r<1\), the map \(x\mapsto q_{\beta}(r,x)\) is convex on \(\mathbb R\). Moreover, for every \(c_0,c_1\in\mathbb R\) and \(0<t<1\), \(\operatorname{Eq}_{\beta,r}(c_0,c_1;t)\) holds if and only if \(r=0\) or \(c_0=c_1\).
body.justification: Convexity supplies the global single-crossing fact needed to optimize over arbitrary compact alternatives.
body.gap: Shenfeld and van Handel prove Gaussian-measure convexity and equality cases but do not derive convexity of conditional selected-score quantiles.
body.consumer: Power calculations need only the least clinically relevant effect coordinate, even when the prespecified alternative set is nonconvex.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(\gamma_2\) denote standard Gaussian measure on \(\mathbb R^2\), and define
\[
\mathcal O(c,z)=[c,\infty)\times[z,\infty),\qquad
\mathcal T(c,z)=Q^{-1}\{Q(c)Q(z)\}.
\]
Minkowski interpolation of two such orthants is the orthant with interpolated thresholds. The Ehrhard--Borell inequality therefore gives
\[
\mathcal T((1-t)c_0+tc_1,(1-t)z_0+tz_1)\le(1-t)\mathcal T(c_0,z_0)+t\mathcal T(c_1,z_1),
\]
because \(Q^{-1}(u)=-\Phi^{-1}(u)\). Thus \(\mathcal T\) is jointly convex. If \(Z\) is standard normal, \(Q(Z)\) is uniform on \((0,1)\), and
\[
\Pr\{\mathcal T(c,Z)>y\}=\frac{Q(y)}{Q(c)},\qquad y>c.
\]
Hence \(\mathcal T(c,Z)\) has the law of a standard normal conditioned to exceed \(c\).

Put \(v=(1-r^2)^{1/2}>0\), \(W(c,z,e)=r\mathcal T(c,z)+ve\), and
\[
\mathcal A(c,q)=\{(z,e):W(c,z,e)\le q\}.
\]
For \(r\ge0\), \(W\) is convex, so
\[
(1-t)\mathcal A(c_0,q_0)+t\mathcal A(c_1,q_1)\subseteq
\mathcal A((1-t)c_0+tc_1,(1-t)q_0+tq_1).
\]
Take \(q_i=q_\beta(r,c_i)\). Each set on the left has Gaussian measure \(1-\beta\). Ehrhard--Borell and the inclusion show that the set on the right has measure at least \(1-\beta\). Since \(vE\) gives a strictly positive continuous density, the generalized quantile is unique, and
\[
q_\beta(r,(1-t)c_0+tc_1)\le(1-t)q_\beta(r,c_0)+tq_\beta(r,c_1).
\]
This is convexity.

If \(r=0\), the quantile is the constant \(\Phi^{-1}(1-\beta)\); if \(c_0=c_1\), chord equality is tautological. Conversely, suppose \(r>0\), \(c_0\ne c_1\), and chord equality holds. Then every inequality in the preceding measure comparison is equality. The equality classification for Ehrhard--Borell says that \(\mathcal A(c_0,q_0)\) and \(\mathcal A(c_1,q_1)\) must be parallel half-spaces or equal up to null sets. They are not half-spaces: their boundary is
\[
e=\{q-r\mathcal T(c,z)\}/v,
\]
and \(\mathcal T(c,z)\to c\) as \(z\to-\infty\) but \(\mathcal T(c,z)\to\infty\) as \(z\to\infty\), so this graph is not affine. If the two closed convex sets are equal up to null sets, they are equal, and their boundary graphs give \(\mathcal T(c_0,z)-\mathcal T(c_1,z)\) constant in \(z\). As \(z\to-\infty\), the constant is \(c_0-c_1\). If it were nonzero, the identity \(Q(\mathcal T(c,z))=Q(c)Q(z)\), together with the elementary Mills bounds \(\phi(x)/(x+x^{-1})<Q(x)<\phi(x)/x\) for \(x>0\), would make the ratio \(Q(\mathcal T(c_0,z))/Q(\mathcal T(c_1,z))\) tend to zero or infinity as \(z\to\infty\), whereas it equals the finite positive constant \(Q(c_0)/Q(c_1)\). Thus the constant is zero and then \(c_0=c_1\), a contradiction. The stated equality cases follow.
